title: Live step of a compiled nondeterministic program
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, $l_0$ an initial label, $D$ a deterministic machine with $k_D$ work tapes, $q_0$ a choice of initial decider states, and $B,W$ natural-number bounds. Suppose the deterministic interpretation of $A$ with choices replaced by $0$, started at label $l$ with register values $v$ and no recorded answer, takes one step to label $l'$ and register values $v'$, still with no recorded answer; suppose the associated precondition holds and $|\mathrm{bits}(v(r)+1)|\le W$ for every register $r$. Then there is a natural number $S$ such that every run of the compiled nondeterministic machine from the corresponding initial configuration using a choice word of length at most $S$ has register-head positions between $-1$ and $W$ and decider-tape head positions of absolute value at most $B$, and every choice word of length exactly $S$ reaches the initial configuration associated with $(l',v')$, preserving the input and output.
hypotheses_covered: A, l₀, D, q₀, B, and W are given
l and l′ are program labels; v and v′ give register values; out is the initial output word
The deterministic interpretation from (l,v,no answer) takes one step to (l′,v′,no answer)
The precondition NPre holds at (l,v,no answer)
For every register r, the bit-word for v(r)+1 has length at most W
